This appeal coming on for admission this day, th e court  following:
 ORDER
With the consent of both learned counsel for the parties, the matter is heard finally at motion stage.
2. This appeal has been filed by the appellant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 against the award dated 13.09.2017 passed in Claim Case No.1800065/2015 by IInd Addl.
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Chhindwara District- Chhindwara (M.P.)

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Chhindwara District- Chhindwara (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
seeking setting aside of impugned award and liability to pay the compensation.
3.

Learned counsel for the appellant, after referring to impugned award as well as evidence on record, submits that Tribunal has wrongly held that respondent- Insurance Company is liable to pay only Rs.1,00,000/- out of total compensation of Rs.9,14,900/-.
It is also urged that in the instant case, deceased was third party and risk of third party was also covered in the Insurance policy.

Therefore, Insurance-Company as well as appellant/driver are jointly and severely liable to pay the compensation.
4.
Learned counsel for the respondents No.1 to 4 submits that he has nothing to argue in the case.

5. Learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company, after referring to para-30 of impugned award, submits that Tribunal has rightly held that in the instant case, Insurance policy is Act policy,
therefore, Insurance-Company is liable to pay compensation to the extent of Rs.1,00,000/-.

Hence,
appeal filed by appellant be dismissed.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
7. Sole issue involved in the case is liability regarding payment of compensation.
Perusal of Insurance policy (Ex.D/1) and deposition of non- applicant witness Anand Swaroop reveal that in the instant case, Insurance policy is only Act policy and not comprehensive/package policy.
8. Learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company has also filed along with Insurance policy Ex.D/1 (IMT).
Perusal of Insurance- policy along with IMT reveal that it is Act policy.
Therefore, Insurance-Company is liable to pay the compensation to the extent of Rs.1,00,000/- and not more than that.

This aspect of the matter has been elaborately dealt by Tribunal in para-30, 31,
32 and 33.

This is also evident from principle laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in (National Asharam vs Smt. Runi Bai on 7 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185937997/
2 Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. Balakrishnan and another 2013 (1) SCC 731 , General Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. M. Laxmi and others 2009 (17) SCC 301 and M.A.No.5762 of 2019 HDFC Ergo General Insurance Company Vs. Smt. Dumri Bai dated 11.07.2022.
9.
